# 1. One public wafer frame, propagation along +y

Date: 2026-11-02

## Status

Accepted (recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-03 from the history and from `docs/FRAME_UNIFICATION_STATUS.md` and `docs/KERNEL_PORT_STATUS.md`).

## Context

Before this decision nyx had several coordinate conventions at once: 2D legacy models in "model axes", a `Frame` field on `Materials`, an `Axes` toggle in the window, wrong 2D labels (y where z was meant), and a positive out-of-plane wave number `k` that meant a wave towards the viewer (-y). A frame adapter translated between the public frame and the kernels' frame, and every new field name had to be placed by a 22-string table.

## Decision

There is one public frame, the **wafer frame**: x lateral, y the direction of propagation, z the surface normal, right-handed. A 2D cross-section is the x-z plane with y into the page. A wave along +y is `exp(-j beta y)` and has positive `k` (`PROP_SIGN = +1`). The time convention is `e^{j omega t}`.

* `femcore::section` is the one place that knows axis numbers: `plane_tensor`, `local_tensor`, `LOCAL_AXES`, `wafer_point`, `PLANE_VOIGT`, field names. Nobody else permutes axes.
* Solid kernels use the Voigt order (x, z, y); mode solvers use the local triple (lateral, normal, propagation), which is left-handed and only reverses the reading of the polarization sense.
* The ring (axisymmetric) kernels use their local wafer frame (r, theta, z) = (x, y, z); `m > 0` is a wave along +theta = +y.
* 2D PML is written along x and z. A y layer on a 2D mesh is refused, with no alias, because y means y in 3D files.
* `Frame`, `Materials::frame`, the adapter, `rename_wafer_fields` and the legacy front-ends were deleted rather than kept as shims: nothing was released.

## Consequences

* All kernels name result fields in wafer axes straight from the kernel (`Ex`, `Ez`, `Ey`, `ux`, `uz`, `uy`, `sxz`, `syz`); a 2D field the table cannot place fails a debug assertion in `solve`.
* Positive `k` changed meaning (cosmetic for elastic frequencies, which are even in `k`); neff did not change, only the sign of `Ey`.
* geom is wafer-native too (`crates/geom/tests/wafer.rs`, `sweep_axes.rs`), so a geom model needs no translation on the way to a mesh.
* The seven failing golden tests (rough spot R22) concern kernels ported under this decision; they fail by machine noise, not by frame errors.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/section.rs`, `solve.rs`, `ems*.rs`, `sms*.rs`, `sbs*.rs`, `dfs.rs`, `ems_pml.rs::cell_stretches`; `crates/geom/src/stack.rs`, `topo3.rs`. History: `4eab426`, `1d51d96`, `dde3caa`, `f2cb8b7`, `35cceba`, `dcb8ff2` to `a0bb492`.

## Contract

`contracts/frames` (`crates/femcore/tests/contracts.rs`, tests `frames_*`) pins the constants and name tables of `section`.
decisions.title: One public wafer frame, propagation along +y

# 10. Golden files are the numerical oracle, and are not regenerated to hide a difference

Date: 2026-11-02

## Status

Accepted (rule in `CLAUDE.md`, a047506). Open: the reference platform and tolerance (R22).

## Context

Porting the kernels to wafer axes (ADR 1) needed an oracle that did not depend on the code being changed. The kernels were run through `solve::solve` before each phase and their outputs frozen.

## Decision

* `crates/femcore/tests/golden_frames/*.json` (read by `tests/golden_frames.rs`, 24 tests) and `crates/geom/golden/*.json` with `*.expected.json` (read by `tests/goldens.rs`; closed-form areas) are the numerical oracle.
* `NYX_WRITE_GOLDEN=1` (femcore) and `GEOM_WRITE_GOLDEN=1` (geom) rewrite them; do so only for a kernel known to be right, and say so in the commit. Never regenerate to make a failing test pass before the cause is understood.
* The golden comparison accepts an eigenvector with all its signed fields negated, because the overall sign of a mode is round-off when two entries tie in modulus.
* Tolerances are per case (1e-9 for `dfs`, 1e-8 to 1e-7 for 2D EM and solid, 1e-6 for Brillouin and rings).

## Consequences

* Seven golden tests fail on main on this machine (Windows, Rust 1.99.1) by ~1e-6 relative, identical with `NYX_THREADS=1`, and already at `35cceba`, the commit that wrote them. The goldens carry the platform of their freezing (CPU, FMA, GEMM blocking). Until the reference platform or a tolerance is decided, new contract tests in this work do not depend on these goldens.
* The ring goldens were written with the kernel of `1f2cb58` and the Brillouin goldens with a kernel that still propagated along -y on the mirrored crystal; they check +y indirectly (displacement along y is mirrored in the files).
* `solid_pml::low_reflecting_boundary_gives_the_analytic_damped_bar_modes` fails before and after the port and has no golden.

## Code

`crates/femcore/tests/golden_frames.rs`, `golden_frames/`, `crates/geom/tests/goldens.rs`, `crates/geom/golden/`.

## Contract

`contracts/frames` and `contracts/kernel_stages` complement the goldens with checks that do not need frozen floating-point values.
decisions.title: Golden files are the numerical oracle, and are not regenerated to hide a difference

# 11. Determinism: fixed chunks, ordered reductions, one thread pool

Date: 2026-10-31

## Status

Accepted. The rule is stated in `CLAUDE.md` ("the same input gives the same numbers") and in `solvers/par.rs`.

## Context

Parallel floating-point sums depend on the order of addition. Results that change with the thread count make goldens, caches and comparisons between runs worthless.

## Decision

* Parallel kernels cut work into **fixed-size chunks independent of the thread count**, compute partials per chunk and fold them **in chunk order**. A result is bit-identical for every thread count and equal to the serial run.
* `femcore::par` owns the one shared rayon pool; `NYX_THREADS=N` sets its size (`1` makes everything serial). `solvers::par` runs on that pool; small problems stay serial because waking a worker costs 50 to 150 microseconds.
* `NYX_PROFILE=1` echoes the solver log.
* `portable-kernels` removes the one known source of cross-machine drift (the faer GEMM restart multiply picks FMA/blocking by CPU); it never mattered between thread counts.

## Consequences

* `meshers::par` uses `std::thread::scope` and `FEMMESH_THREADS` instead of the pool (R03). The chunk rule is the same, so results agree, but the thread count is controlled by a different variable.
* Determinism is across threads, not across machines: see ADR 10.
* Tests: `tests/determinism.rs`, `tests/solvers/determinism`, and bit-identical reruns in the mesher tests.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/par.rs`, `solvers/par.rs`.

## Contract

Covered by the existing determinism tests; `contracts/kernel_stages` does not repeat them.

## Amendment 2026-11-04 (mesh phase)

The mesher's own `par` module is gone: its fixed-chunk reductions (`CHUNK`, `fold_chunks_mut`, `sum_range`) moved into `femcore::par`, and the metric adaptation now takes its thread count from `femcore::par::threads()` (`NYX_THREADS`, at most 32); `FEMMESH_THREADS` no longer exists. Results are bit-identical for any thread count by the chunk rule, so nothing but the variable name changes (R03 is resolved for the mesher; the solver library keeps `solvers/par.rs`).
decisions.title: Determinism: fixed chunks, ordered reductions, one thread pool

# 12. Physics modules carry three-letter codes

Date: 2026-11-03

## Status

Accepted (Paul's choice; commit `d2e0f74`).

Superseded in part by ADR 24: the code `sbs` and its modules are gone.

## Context

Module names mixed physics and implementation history (`scalar`, `solid`, `emw`, `brillouin`, `ring_brillouin`) and the same words meant different things in different crates (`solvers::scalar` is the solver library's scalar trait).

## Decision

| Code | Physics | Modules |
|---|---|---|
| `dfs` | scalar diffusion (electrostatics, heat) | `dfs` |
| `sms` | solid mechanics | `sms`, `sms_pml`, `sms_floquet`, `sms_lrb`, `sms_kz`, `sms_axisym` |
| `ems` | EM waves | `ems`, `ems_pml`, `ems3d`, `ems_axisym` |
| `sbs` | stimulated Brillouin scattering | `sbs`, `sbs_ring` |

New physics modules are named the same way: three letters, then a suffix for the variant. The public `Physics` enum is unchanged (`Electrostatics`, `Heat`, `Solid`, `Emw`, `Brillouin`); the codes name modules, not the type.

## Consequences

* The rename left comments, timer labels and test file names with the old prefixes (`emw3d`, `emw_pml`, `solid_pml`) (R13).
* `periodic.rs` and `analysis.rs`/`polarization.rs` are not under a code. `periodic` is used by `sms_floquet` and `ems3d`, so it belongs to no single physics.
* The codes are unrelated to the three-letter names of the kernel stages.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/{dfs,sms*,ems*,sbs*}.rs`, `lib.rs` module list, `docs/KERNEL_PORT_STATUS.md` table.

## Contract

None needed beyond compilation; the module list is part of `contracts/kernel_stages`.
decisions.title: Physics modules carry three-letter codes

# 13. Pure Rust; nothing Python ships; HDF5 is optional; the toolchain is pinned

Date: 2026-10-28

## Status

Accepted (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, a047506).

## Context

nyx is a desktop application for researchers on Windows. Python and C dependencies make it hard to build, ship and reproduce. Two parts of the ported work were developed against Python or C tools (the SLEPc comparison harness, HDF5).

## Decision

* The application, library and MCP server are pure Rust. `*.py` is git-ignored on purpose. Any GDS layout is built with gdsfactory, never raw gdstk (Paul's rule; this is a layout-tool rule, not a build dependency).
* HDF5/XDMF results are behind the `hdf5-metno` feature of `femcore` (`hdf5` in `app`; `phdf5` adds MPI-IO). They need the HDF5 library; the default build does not.
* `faer` supplies dense/sparse linear algebra, `spade` the Delaunay triangulation, `quick-xml` the project XML, `serde`/`serde_json` the data model, `rayon` the pool, `egui`/`eframe` the window. Projects save as JSON or XML (`.nyx.json`, `.nyx.xml`) from the same serde value (`xmlio`).
* `rust-toolchain.toml` pins the compiler; `Cargo.toml` says `rust-version = 1.84`. Always build with `--release`: the solvers are unusably slow unoptimised.

## Consequences

* The state of the checks depends on the toolchain: clippy `-D warnings` is not clean with 1.99.1 and `cargo fmt --check` fails widely (R23).
* XML is a derived encoding of a serde value, not a schema of its own: field names of the Rust types are the file format, and nothing versions them (R20).
* The ports' Python harnesses live outside this repository.

## Code

`Cargo.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `crates/femcore/Cargo.toml`, `crates/femcore/src/xmlio.rs`, `h5io.rs`, `crates/app/src/batch.rs`.

## Contract

`contracts/problem_spec` exercises the JSON and XML encodings of the `ProblemSpec` part of a project; a contract for the whole `Project` is not written (it lives in the `app` crate, R16).
decisions.title: Pure Rust; nothing Python ships; HDF5 is optional; the toolchain is pinned

# 14. Work is stored as workflows: JSON manifests, an append-only run log and deterministic `.nyx` archives

Date: 2026-11-01

## Status

**Amended by ADR 39, 59, 63 and 65 (spec file names, no femcore dependency).** Accepted by implementation (`93321f5` nyx-store, `3dd760f` design and mockups, `37e5871` wired into the app). The open questions of `docs/WORKFLOWS_DESIGN.md` section 11 (should runs of different specs mix in one experiment?) are open.

## Context

Researchers iterate: change a width, re-run, compare. Autosaved project files in `nyx_runs` did not say which work belonged together, could not be searched, and could not be shared as one unit.

## Decision

* The unit of work is a **workflow**: a folder holding `workflow.json` (manifest: experiments, tags, status), `history.jsonl` (one line per version of the set-up), `notes.md`, `specs/` and one folder per experiment. Workflows live under a workspace folder (`workspace.json`, default `Documents/nyx`).
* **JSON, not XML,** for manifests and runs: faster, appendable, trivial for MCP. The experiment's **spec stays the project XML** (`.nyx.xml`), so existing projects and their round-trip tests keep working.
* Runs are **append-only** lines in `runs.jsonl` (`RunRecord`: id, time, seconds, status, spec hash, version of the set-up, parameters, metrics, tags, star, note, artifacts, error); a digest is derived from them. Metrics come from `SolveResult` (`runs::metrics_of`): n_eff, first scalar, TE fraction, dof count, every numeric scalar in snake_case.
* A `.nyx` file is **one deterministic small ZIP** with an `ArchiveManifest` (format, kind, level, nyx version, files); import is a safe extraction (no path escapes). Three share levels: recipe (default), results, meshes.
* The **concept card** (family, dimensions, physics, study, wavelength, materials inferred from refractive index) is generated from the spec, never typed; search uses plain words with a synonym table and numbers with units.
* Everything is plain serde with ordered maps so files are byte-for-byte reproducible. blake3 hashes identify specs.
* Nothing is deleted by rules; "Done" leaves the dashboard at once; a 12-card cap and drafts that never touch disk.

## Consequences

* `nyx-store` knows `ProblemSpec` and `Project` only through untyped values read tolerantly, so a newer spec still opens, and a changed layout is silently unseen (R25 is exactly this).
* `RunRecord.femcore` is filled from the wrong crate's version (R21).
* The store depends on all of `femcore` for two items (R15).
* `workflow.json` carries its format under the key `nyx` (`FORMAT = 1`) and `WorkflowDir::open` refuses a newer one with "made with a newer nyx"; the archive manifest has a `format` too. Its `version` key is the number of the current set-up version, not a format number. No migration code exists.

## Code

`crates/nyx-store/src/*`, `crates/app/src/{shell,wfview,sheets}.rs`, `docs/WORKFLOWS_DESIGN.md`. History: `93321f5`, `3dd760f`, `959d1d5`, `37e5871`, `2b5b66a`, `b5e5bfb`.

## Contract

`contracts/store` (`crates/nyx-store/tests/contracts.rs`): exemplar `workflow.json` and `runs.jsonl` line must round-trip, an old run line without the later keys must still read, a newer manifest must be refused, the metric names of a `SolveResult` are pinned, and the concept-card contract is written and `#[ignore]`d pending R25. The archive manifest is not covered yet.
decisions.title: Work is stored as workflows: JSON manifests, an append-only run log and deterministic `.nyx` archives

# 15. The AI interface is a separate workspace with a hand-written stdio MCP server

Date: 2026-11-01

## Status

**Superseded in part by ADR 26, 28 and 57 (see ADR 65).** Accepted (`docs/MCP_ASSISTANT_PLAN.md` sections 18 to 20; code brought under version control in `36f6b3d`; Connect menu `839efa1`).

Superseded in part by ADR 26: `ai/` is no longer a separate workspace; its crates are in `crates/` and the root workspace.

Superseded in part by ADR 28: the Connect logic exists once, in `nyx-connect`; the app has no copy (R07 resolved).

## Context

An AI host should be able to build a geometry, mesh it, define a problem, solve and pick a mode, with nyx deciding *how* and the AI deciding *what*. The plan was written under the constraint that `app` and `femcore` stay untouched.

## Decision

* The code lives in `ai/`, **its own Cargo workspace** with its own lockfile and target: `nyx-session` (typed tools, knows nothing of MCP), `nyx-mcp` (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, newline-delimited, logs on stderr), `nyx-connect` (detect hosts, write or remove the `nyx` entry with a backup, test the server).
* The server is **hand-written**: no async runtime, no SDK. The subset needed (initialize, tools, resources, progress, cancel) is small, and an SDK would add a dependency tree to a repository whose `geom` is serde-only.
* Each tool has a **parameter table** (`params.rs`) from which the JSON Schema is produced, arguments validated, defaults filled and every assumed value recorded in a **ledger**. Parameters carry a `Matters` rating: high ones are asked for when missing (`status: needs_input`), the others are assumed and listed. `use_defaults: true` accepts the stated fallback.
* **Content-hashed handles**: `g_`, `m_`, `p_`, `r_` plus the FNV-1a digest of the inputs, so repeating a request returns the same handle without recomputing. A journal (`journal.jsonl`), the geom JSON of every geometry (`g_*.geom.json`) and a digest of every result are written to the session folder; meshes and results stay in memory.
* Units are SI everywhere. The reference check is oxide-clad 500 x 300 nm on 2 um BOX: TE0 2.6718, TM0 2.3338.
* "One owner per session": a nyx window and `nyx-mcp` must not both own a session. The agent and the window run in one light process; every solve can run in a detached worker so a host exit does not kill a large solve (settled in plan section 20). Local models: detect and guide only.
* The Connect menu in `app` registers `nyx-mcp` with Claude Code (`~/.claude.json`) and Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`), keeps a `.nyx-backup` copy and leaves other keys alone.

## Consequences

* `Project` is still defined in `app`, so the session cannot read or write a project file (R16).
* The Connect logic exists twice, in `app/src/connect.rs` and `ai/nyx-connect` (R07); `nyx-connect` also handles Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf.
* `CLAUDE.md` and `ai/README.md` say the workspace depends on `femcore` and `geom`; `nyx-session` depends on `femcore` only (R17).
* The tool list and schemas are an external contract with every host that has registered `nyx` (contract `mcp_tools`).

## Code

`ai/nyx-session/src/{tools,params,workspace,guide}.rs`, `ai/nyx-mcp/src/main.rs`, `ai/nyx-connect/src/*`, `crates/app/src/connect.rs`.

## Contract

`contracts/mcp_tools` (`ai/nyx-mcp/tests/contracts.rs`): the names, access annotations and input-schema property names of the tools, snapshotted.
decisions.title: The AI interface is a separate workspace with a hand-written stdio MCP server

# 16. `.fmsh`: a lossless, self-checking binary format for meshes and results

Date: 2026-10-28

## Status

Accepted by the mesher port (`docs/ports/meshers/STATUS.md` "Decisions I made"). The format has no consumer in the app yet; HDF5/XDMF (`h5io`) remains the app's results format.

## Context

The original mesher stack used HDF5 plus a small XML descriptor. HDF5 needs the C library or an unproven pure-Rust writer; VTK and text writers produce large files; the requirement was no loss of information.

## Decision

`.fmsh` (version 2) is one self-describing, CRC-checked file holding a mixed-cell mesh (cell types, labels, boundary facets) and any number of result steps with named point or cell fields. Floats round-trip bit for bit. Each array is stored with the smallest of byte planes, XOR-with-previous or dictionary coding, then an adaptive range coder (order 0, order 1 or raw), implemented in `io/entropy.rs` with no dependency. Sizes are 12 to 30 times smaller than plain binary on structured and PML meshes, 2.1 times on an adapted mesh, and within 7 percent of `xz -9e`. A lossy quantised option was deliberately not added.

## Consequences

* Not wired to the MCP plan's "mesh not stored in v1; rebuilt deterministically" (a row of the session table in `MCP_ASSISTANT_PLAN.md`) or to `nyx-store`'s `Meshes` share level, which could use it.
* The connectivity of adapted meshes (5.5 bytes per triangle) could drop about 4 times with a topological coder; not done.
* Three results/mesh encodings exist: `.fmsh`, HDF5/XDMF (`h5io`, attr `version = 2`) and the project XML/JSON; `.fmsh` (version byte 2) and the HDF5 file (attribute `version = 2`) record a version, the project encodings do not.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/meshers/io/{fmsh,entropy}.rs`, `h5io.rs`.

## Contract

`contracts/mesh` includes an `.fmsh` round-trip and a pinned version byte (`mesh_fmsh_round_trip_and_version`).
decisions.title: `.fmsh`: a lossless, self-checking binary format for meshes and results

# 17. Element sizes come from the physics of the problem

Date: 2026-11-02

## Status

Accepted as opt-in (`e5fad41`, `12042b4`; app option `e950f05`, checkbox `aa513ea`). Defaults are starting values calibrated on smooth modes only.

## Context

A mesh that resolves a wave needs a fixed number of points per wavelength in each material; a mesh for a high-index core must be finer than one for the cladding, and elastic modes depend on the slowest anisotropic plane wave. Users were choosing element sizes by hand.

## Decision

`physics_size` derives an element size per domain from the study: wavelength of EM modes and eigenfrequencies (n times shorter in index-n material), slowest anisotropic plane wave for solid eigenfrequencies, Brillouin (optical and acoustic), with **12 points per wavelength for order 1 and 6 for order 2**, PML relaxation and eigenfrequency headroom. `meshing::mesh_for_problem` intersects this metric with the geometry metric (2D); `physics_size::adapt_tets` does the same graded in 3D. Estimators (`estimate::Estimator::{combine, e_field}`) treat E components as one vector field with one metric.

## Consequences

* Only order 1 and 2 are covered; points per wavelength for higher orders are unmeasured (`MISSING_FEATURES.md` section 1).
* No test runs a Brillouin or ring study on a sized mesh; sharp corners, thin layers and high contrast are uncalibrated.
* The app shows the option as one checkbox on the model editor (`GeometrySpec::physics_sizing`), with no report of the sizes it used and no per-domain override.
* `physics_size` reads `ProblemSpec`, so the mesher depends on the problem types, and a change in `Study`/`BrillouinSpec` field names reaches the mesher.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/physics_size.rs`, `meshing.rs`, `estimate.rs`, `crates/app/src/state.rs`. History: `e5fad41`, `12042b4`, `e950f05`, `aa513ea`.

## Contract

`contracts/problem_spec` (the field names `physics_size` reads: `Study::{Modes, Eigenfrequency}`, `BrillouinSpec::wavelength`, `Materials`).
decisions.title: Element sizes come from the physics of the problem

# 18. Curved elements are deferred; the mesher projects onto exact geometry but stores no curved nodes

Date: 2026-11-02

## Status

Accepted as a constraint (paul, 2026-11-02, quoted in `docs/ports/meshers/FEATURE_DEPENDENCIES.md`). Open: node-storage convention, Jacobian checks and maximum order on the solver side.

## Context

Cells are straight-sided (constant gradients), so any curved boundary carries an O(h^2) geometric error whatever the element order; for P2 and Nedelec-2 this is the accuracy ceiling for discs, rings and spheres (`GEOMETRY_ARCHITECTURE.md` problem 6).

## Decision

* Curved nodes are **not stored yet**. Until the solvers define a convention, the mesher (a) places boundary and interface vertices on the exact geom edge or face (`GeomOracle2` in 2D, `geom3` in 3D) and (b) will do Jacobian validity checks and projection of mid-edge nodes onto the exact geometry when asked.
* The mesher assumes **no maximum element order** and assumes both Nedelec families.
* The curved-element refactor of the solvers belongs to the integration session, benchmarked against closed forms (`GEOM_HANDOFF.md` decision 6); geom's job is to make it possible.
* `matfree.rs` in the ported solver library (sum-factorised high-order operators for curved hexahedra) needs nyx's element geometry and is the intended consumer.

## Consequences

* `MISSING_FEATURES.md` section 1: no stored high-order nodes, no Jacobian checks for curved hex/prism/tet, no projection of mid-edge nodes. The 3D oracle can project but nothing places nodes.
* Smooth analytic surfaces (sphere, SDF projectors) are unit-tested but no end-to-end test adapts a curved body and checks convergence of a solver quantity.
* A format that stores curved nodes will change `SimplexMesh`/`CellMesh` and `.fmsh`; contracts `mesh` and `kernel_stages` are written so such a change fails loudly and is versioned (ADR 19).

## Code

`crates/geom/src/query.rs`, `curve.rs`; `crates/femcore/src/meshing.rs::GeomOracle2`, `meshers/adapt/geom.rs`, `geom3.rs`; `solvers/matfree.rs`.

## Contract

`contracts/mesh` states that meshes carry vertices only (test `mesh_has_no_curved_node_storage`).
decisions.title: Curved elements are deferred; the mesher projects onto exact geometry but stores no curved nodes

# 19. Interfaces that outlive a run are pinned by exemplar files and contract tests, and carry a version

Date: 2026-11-03

## Status

Accepted by this change (the tests and exemplars are in the same commit). Adding a `format` key to `Project` and `FeatureList` is **proposed, not done** (it alters every saved file).

## Context

Saved projects, `specs/` files, `workflow.json`, `runs.jsonl`, geom feature lists, `.fmsh` files and the MCP tool list are read by code that was not built together with the code that wrote them: later versions of nyx, nyx-store reading specs as untyped values, AI hosts that registered `nyx` weeks ago. serde reads leniently (unknown keys ignored, `#[serde(default)]` keys filled in), so a renamed or dropped field does not fail; it silently loses a setting (ROUGH_SPOTS R20). Only `workflow.json`, `.fmsh` and the HDF5 file had a version gate.

## Decision

1. Each interface has a **contract**: a checked-in exemplar under `docs/architecture/contracts/<name>.v<N>.json` (or a snapshot built from the running program for the MCP tool list) and a test that produces the same bytes from the code (`crates/femcore/tests/contracts.rs`, `crates/geom/tests/contracts.rs`, `crates/nyx-store/tests/contracts.rs`, `ai/nyx-mcp/tests/contracts.rs`). The exemplar is the schema; a separate JSON Schema would need a validator dependency and a second thing to keep in step.
2. A contract test fails on **any** change of the interface, additive or not. The failure message points here. Changing the exemplar (`NYX_WRITE_CONTRACT=1`, same convention as the goldens in ADR 10) is a deliberate act that goes together with an entry in `docs/architecture/contracts/VERSIONS.md`:
   * **additive** (new optional key with a default, new tool, new optional argument): bump the minor, keep reading old files;
   * **breaking** (rename, removal, changed meaning or unit, new required key, changed node order or label base): bump the major, add a reader for the previous major or state that old files are refused, and say so in the commit.
3. Behaviour that the interfaces *rely on* but that is not a data shape is pinned too: the label bases of meshes, the node order of quadrilaterals, the `.fmsh` version byte, the wafer-frame constants of `section`, the string `"cancelled"`, the set of public kernel-stage functions.
4. Contract tests do **not** use frozen floating-point results; those are the goldens of ADR 10 and currently fail on this machine (R22). Contract tests must pass on any platform.
5. A contract that exposes a known defect is written anyway and `#[ignore]`d with the rough-spot number in the reason (`store_card_reads_current_project`, R25). `cargo test -- --include-ignored` shows it failing.
6. Stable identity rule, recorded once: spec and file identity inside nyx-store is blake3 over the bytes; AI-session handles are FNV-1a over the inputs; geom caching uses geom's own content signature. They are not interchangeable.

## Consequences

* A reviewer sees an interface change as a diff of one JSON file plus a line in `VERSIONS.md`.
* The exemplars are not a JSON Schema; they do not say which keys are optional. The tests that exercise leniency (`problem_spec_reading_is_lenient_in_both_directions`, `store_run_record_exemplar_is_stable_and_old_lines_still_read`) document what is optional today.
* Proposed next steps, each its own change: a `format` key on `Project` and `FeatureList` read by a migration function; a contract crate holding `ProblemSpec`, `SolveResult`, `Project` and `xmlio` (R15, R16, R27); a contract for the archive manifest and for the `.nyx.xml` encoding of a `Project`.

## Code

## Contract

This ADR is the rule; `docs/architecture/contracts/README.md` lists the contracts and how to run them.

# 2. Geometry is a serialisable feature list addressed by names and selectors

Date: 2026-10-31

## Status

Accepted. Decisions 1 to 5 of `docs/GEOM_HANDOFF.md` section 0 are Paul's ("do not reopen").

## Context

The earlier code had three unrelated geometry languages (`Rectangle`, `Block`, `Shapes`, `Solids` plus `extrude` and bbox relabels), boundary numbers that depended on creation order, labels assigned after meshing by nearest chain segment, and domain numbers hard-coded in the use cases (SOI 1/2/3, chips 1-4, PML 11-15, 21-22, 41-45). See `docs/GEOMETRY_ARCHITECTURE.md` section 1 for the ten specific problems.

## Decision

* The model of a geometry is one flat, serialisable **feature list** (`geom::model::FeatureList`) with named parameters and expressions. The Rust builder, the GUI form and "Copy as Rust" all edit or print this same data: code-first and GUI are equivalent.
* A model evaluates to a **region complex**: named regions with shared interface faces, produced by one n-ary arrangement plus a CSG expression, so union, difference and intersection are one algorithm.
* **Names, not numbers.** Every region, edge and face descends from one primitive role. Boundary conditions, materials, mesh sizes, periodic pairs and PML attach through **selectors** (a small serialisable rule language). Integers exist only as a compiled output, `LabelMap`, which is what the solvers read.
* Parameters are shared by name, so sweeps are one call and sliders drive the same data.

## Consequences

* All geometry in the app is a geom model (`ffa1bf6` removed rectangle, block, shapes, solids). Use cases build geom models (`usecases/soi.rs`, `bragg.rs`, `chips.rs`).
* Boundary conditions can stay valid when a shape is inserted; the GUI can show "click a boundary, get the rules that pick it" (`9b49399`).
* `Bc.labels: Vec<i32>` remains in `ProblemSpec`; it is the compiled form and is stable only for one evaluation of one model (a limitation of the interface, see contract `problem_spec`).
* Persistent naming makes the saved model, not the mesh, the artefact that is versioned and hashed (`nyx-store`, `nyx-session` handles).

## Code

`crates/geom/src/{model,eval,labels,select,sim,print,diff}.rs`, `crates/femcore/src/geomdrive.rs`, `crates/app/src/{geomui,state}.rs`. History: `08dd007`, `ffa1bf6`, `4a3cb55`, `5ebb4dd`, `bfa09c1`, `9b49399`.

## Contract

`contracts/geom_model`: exemplar feature lists in `crates/geom/golden/*.json` already evaluate to closed-form expectations (`tests/goldens.rs`); `crates/geom/tests/contracts.rs` adds the byte-exact JSON round trip of the exemplars and the dependency rule of ADR 3.

# 20. Version control: a branch per task, never on main, a jj workspace per working session, status files as handoffs

Date: 2026-11-03

## Status

Accepted (`CLAUDE.md`, commit `a047506`; paul wants jj used, 2026-11-03).

Refined by ADR 27: the restructure runs in the repository `nyx2`, one jj workspace per working session.

## Context

nyx is built by many short working sessions, human and AI, on one machine, with `main` local and unpushed. Work was lost or tangled when sessions shared one working copy: a thread "switched the shared `nyx-jj` working copy mid-session" (`MISSING_FEATURES.md` section 6), uncommitted `geom` and `ai/` trees lived only in the main checkout for days (`CAPABILITIES_MEMO.md`, section 0.1).

* Each working session uses its **own jj workspace** (`jj workspace add ../<name>`), not the shared clone `nyx-jj`.
* `docs/*_STATUS.md` files are the handoff between sessions: read the relevant one before starting, update it before finishing.
* Nothing is left only in an uncommitted working tree or a side folder.
* `runs/`, `dist/` and results are git-ignored and never committed. `NYX_WRITE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites are committed only with a statement that the kernel is known to be right (ADR 10).
* Build artefacts: `target/` is local; `ai/` has its own `target` and lockfile.

## Consequences

* `main` is a local branch with no remote; "pushed" is not available as a safety net. Git bundles of earlier branches (`kernel-port*.bundle`, `physics-codes.bundle`) sit in `nyx-jj/target`; they are the only off-branch copies I saw.
* Two checkouts exist beside the jj clone: `nyx` (the git main checkout, with two untracked docs, R24) and `nyx-main-checkout-backup-2026-11-01`.
* This architecture work lives on the bookmark `arch-model-adrs` in the workspace `nyx-arch`.

## Code

`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/*_STATUS.md`, `.gitignore`.

## Contract

None. The rule is process, not a data shape.

# 21. Polarization of an optical mode is computed from its complex fields, in the solvers' local frame

Date: 2026-10-31

## Status

Accepted (commit `4107cfa`, "Analysis tab, ring and 3D polarization"; `e60ad11` for the first version). `docs/photonic_use_cases.md` is the description.

Superseded in part by ADR 24: the Brillouin study no longer produces an analysis; the optical mode set moved to `femcore::optical`.

## Context

Users of waveguide mode solvers want to know whether a mode is quasi-TE, quasi-TM, hybrid or circular. The plotted fields are real and lose the phase between components, so they cannot give the Stokes parameters of hybrid or leaky modes. Degenerate modes (the square 300 nm wire in oxide has an exactly degenerate TE/TM pair) come out of the eigensolver as arbitrary mixtures, so their individual polarizations mean nothing.

## Decision

* `analysis` and `polarization` work from the **complex fields the solver found at quadrature points** (with area weights), not from plotted fields. Every optical mode solver returns `SolveResult::analysis` next to its fields: the 2D mode solver (real, complex with PML or a tilted crystal), the 3D eigenmode solver, the Brillouin study of a straight guide (pump and Stokes) and of a ring (whispering-gallery modes).
* Per mode: integrated Stokes vector, a point on the Poincare sphere, degree of polarization, ellipticity and orientation, the TE and longitudinal energy shares, and a class (quasi-TE, quasi-TM, linear +-45, elliptical, circular, hybrid).
* **Degenerate modes** (effective indices within 5e-4, or frequencies within 1e-6 relative) form a group; the analysis reports the group Stokes vector (independent of the mixture) and the resolved pair of definite x/y polarization.
* The **sense of rotation** is defined by what can be seen (`S3 > 0`: the E vector turns counter-clockwise as time advances), not by a time convention. Left-handed axis triples (rings, wafer-frame 3D) flip the sign convention.
* The axes of the analysis are the local frame of the mode solvers: x lateral (quasi-TE), **y the surface normal (quasi-TM), z the propagation axis**. In the wafer frame these are x, z and y.

## Consequences

* A second naming of axes lives in the analysis, its documentation and the Analysis tab (x, y normal, z propagation), beside the public wafer frame of ADR 1 (R28).
* `SolveResult` carries an `Option<Analysis>`, so the result type depends on the analysis module (R27).
* `nyx-store::runs::metrics_of` reads `te_fraction` from the analysis rows.
* The class thresholds are heuristics; no closed-form benchmark other than the slab and the square wire exists (tests in `tests/photonics.rs`, `polarization` unit tests).

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/analysis.rs`, `polarization.rs`, `ems.rs`, `ems_pml.rs`, `ems3d.rs`, `sbs.rs`, `sbs_ring.rs`; `crates/app/src/tabs.rs` (Analysis tab); `docs/photonic_use_cases.md`. History: `e60ad11`, `4107cfa`.

## Contract

None of its own. `contracts/solve_result` notes that `analysis` is part of the result.
decisions.title: Polarization of an optical mode is computed from its complex fields, in the solvers' local frame

# 23. The app is a shell over one saved Project: jobs on worker threads, the same code headless

Date: 2026-10-28

## Status

**Superseded by ADR 57 (see ADR 65).** Accepted by practice (`6de7458`, `2b5b66a`, `37e5871`). The plan to move `Project` out of the app (MCP plan, phase 0) was not carried out (R16).

## Context

A researcher edits a model, meshes, solves, looks at results and iterates; the same model must also run on a workstation or cluster without a window, and be driven by tests and screenshot scripts.

## Decision

* `state::Project` is what is saved: `GeometrySpec` (a geom `FeatureList`, global element size `h`, optional extrusion layers, `adapt_scale`, `physics_sizing`), one `ProblemSpec` per physics, the active physics and the colour map. It is written as XML through `xmlio` or JSON. `ResultView` wraps a `SolveResult` with plot state.
* `App` holds the project, the mesh in use (`Doc`), the results and the viewport. Anything slow (building a mesh, opening a file, solving) is a numbered **job on its own thread**; only one runs at a time, and a message for a job that is no longer current cannot end the busy state. A solve has a `Progress` handle: the toolbar shows its stage and a Cancel button (Esc too), and the stage log is part of the result.
* A solve writes the results file requested in the study and an **autosave** of the run (project XML, stage log, optionally HDF5) to the runs folder as `temp_untitled_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`.
* **Headless**: `nyx --batch PROJECT.nyx.xml [--physics ...] [--output serial|parallel FILE.h5]` runs the same code as the window; in a parallel (MPI) run every process solves the whole problem and writes its own block of rows. `nyx --script "cmd; cmd"` drives the window for tests and screenshots (`example N`, `compute`, `shot`, ...). `App::with_context` builds the state without a window for tests.
* The viewport splits drawing by what changes (data, rotation, camera) and caches each part (`scene.rs`), on the shared thread pool.
* The workflow dashboard and workspace live beside this in `shell`, `wfview`, `sheets`, backed by `nyx-store` (ADR 14); the Connect menu registers the MCP server (ADR 15).

## Consequences

* The session layer (`ai/`) cannot load or save a `Project` because the type is in a binary crate (R16).
* The number of the project file's `version` (1) is not read anywhere (R20).
* `app.rs` (about 1.1k lines) and `tabs.rs` hold most behaviour; the workflow design anticipated a refactor of about 2,800 lines (`WORKFLOWS_DESIGN.md` risk 7).
* One job at a time means a long Brillouin solve blocks a mesh rebuild; detached workers are planned for AI sessions (ADR 15).

## Code

`crates/app/src/{main,app,state,worker,batch,script,examples,tabs,geomui,viewport,scene,colormap,theme,kit,dashboard,shell,wfview,sheets,connect}.rs`.

## Contract

`contracts/project` is not written: the exemplar for the saved project would have to live in the app crate. The `ProblemSpec` part is `contracts/problem_spec`.

# 25. A physics is a crate behind the `Physics` trait; the problem is an envelope; the registry is built from cargo features

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted by paul on 2026-11-03 as the target structure (restructure plan, section 2); crate names are gate G3 (default: as written). Implemented as an interface in the foundation phase; the kernels move in phase 4. Supersedes in part ADR 4 (`SimplexMesh` is still the solver contract until phase 2, but physics take it through the alias `Mesh`) and ADR 8 (the ported solver library is wired in phase 3).

## Context

Adding a physics meant touching the shared `Physics` enum, the shared `ProblemSpec` (every physics-specific option lived in it: `out_of_plane`, `thermal`, `plane`, `brillouin`, ...), `solve::dispatch`, the window tabs, the MCP tools, the mesher's sizing and the store's concept card (ROUGH_SPOTS R10, R11, R12, R15). paul's goals 1, 2, 7 and 10: a new physics must not touch the rest of the codebase; window and MCP have the same capabilities; a project loads one to three physics; physics are compiled in.

## Decision

* `nyx-physics` holds the interface and nothing else of any physics: the `Physics` trait, `Ctx` (progress, cancel, imported fields, a `LabelResolver`), the `ProblemSpec` envelope, the descriptors, `SolveResult`, `Error` (with `Cancelled`), the `Registry`, structural validation and generated JSON Schemas.
* A physics is a crate: `nyx-dfs`, `nyx-sms`, `nyx-ems` (three-letter codes, ADR 12). It owns the typed form of its study, condition and option parameters, its kernels (assemble, solve, fields stay public, ADR 9) and its descriptors.
* **The envelope** is `{ physics, order, study: { kind, params }, materials: { region -> material }, bcs: [{ on, kind, params }], params }`. `params` objects are `serde_json::Value` at the interface and are validated against the descriptors (`validate_spec`): unknown keys, wrong types and out-of-range values are errors with plain messages. There is no `format` key until phase 8.
* **Names, not numbers.** Regions and boundaries are `geom` names and selectors (ADR 2); the engine supplies a `LabelResolver` in `Ctx` that turns them into mesh labels (numbered from 1 after phase 2). A material is a name or, until phase 6, inline scalar properties by descriptor name (`MaterialAssign`).
* **Descriptors** (`studies`, `bc_kinds`, `properties`, `params`, `fields`, `exports`, `imports`, `sizing`) are plain serde data; the window builds forms from them, the MCP server builds its schemas from them, the mesher reads the sizing hint. Deviation from the plan's trait: a `params()` method describes the physics-level options of the envelope (plane assumption, thickness, inactive regions); the plan listed `params` in the envelope but no descriptor for it.
* **Couplings** are one-way field links: a physics `exports` fields under a `role` and `imports` a role; `Registry::solve_order` orders a chain and refuses a cycle. Two-way coupling is later.
* **Only plain data crosses the trait** (flat arrays for fields and meshes), so a separate-process plug-in remains possible.
* **The registry is built by the engine from cargo features** (`dfs`, `sms`, `ems`, default all). Nothing outside the physics crates names a physics (checked by the layering test, ADR 26).
* `Mesh` is `femcore::mesh::Mesh`, an alias of `SimplexMesh` today. Phase 2 changes what it is; code outside femcore names it only through `nyx_physics::Mesh`.
* Until phase 4, the physics crates answer `solve` with `Error::NotYetMoved`. Their descriptors are a first version read from the current kernels and `ProblemSpec`, to be refined by the phase 4 owner under the version rules of ADR 19.

## Consequences

* A new physics is one crate plus one line in `nyx-engine`. The window and MCP server list it without code.
* `Ctx` still holds femcore's `Progress`, which kernels reach through a thread-local (R19); phase 4 makes it explicit.
* The sizing hint is `fn sizing(&self, spec)`; to compute wavelengths it needs the materials, which are names until phase 6 resolves them. The phase 4 or 6 owner may add a materials argument; that is a version bump of `physics_api`.
* `SolveResult` is serialisable (R27 resolved at the interface); it does not carry an analysis (ADR 21 is superseded in part by phase 5).
* Descriptor content for the three physics is a first version and not authoritative until phase 4.

## Code

`crates/nyx-physics/**`, `crates/nyx-dfs/**`, `crates/nyx-sms/**`, `crates/nyx-ems/**`, `crates/nyx-engine/src/lib.rs`, `crates/femcore/src/mesh.rs` (the `Mesh` alias).

## Contract

`problem_spec.v2.json`, `solve_result.v2.json`, `physics_descriptors.v1.json`, `physics_dfs.v1.json`, `physics_sms.v1.json`, `physics_ems.v1.json`; the trait surface is pinned by `crates/nyx-physics/tests/contracts.rs` (`the_physics_trait_is_object_safe_and_has_these_methods`).
decisions.title: A physics is a crate behind the `Physics` trait; the problem is an envelope; the registry is built from cargo features

# 26. One Cargo workspace for everything, and a test that holds the crate layering

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (foundation of the restructure, following the plan's "`ai/` joins the root workspace"). Supersedes ADR 15 in part (the separate `ai/` workspace).

## Context

`ai/` was a separate Cargo workspace "so that nothing in `../crates` is touched" (ADR 15). That gave it its own lockfile and target directory, two `nyx-connect` copies (R07), and a build graph nobody could check as a whole (R18). Separately, `cargo test --workspace` showed that `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature, switched on by the app and `nyx-connect`, changes the key order of JSON objects in the test binaries: seventeen golden tests and the MCP tool-list contract compared text or key lists and failed for that reason alone.

## Decision

* `nyx-session`, `nyx-mcp`, `nyx-connect` live in `crates/` and are members of the root workspace; `ai/` is gone. One lockfile, one `cargo test --workspace`.
* `.cargo/config.toml` sets `target-dir = "../nyx2-target"`, a sibling folder, so every jj workspace of the repository (ADR 27) shares the compiled registry dependencies. Cargo serialises builds in one directory; the cost is waiting for the lock, the gain is disk (a target is 3 GB and the machine had 17 GB free).
* `crates/nyx-engine/tests/layering.rs` holds the dependency table of the target structure (plan section 2) and a short `TEMPORARY` list of edges that exist today with the phase that removes each. A new dependency between workspace crates fails the test until the table is changed on purpose; a `TEMPORARY` row whose edge is gone fails too. Nothing but the engine may depend on a physics crate; `femcore` depends on no nyx crate.
* **Tests never compare JSON text or key order.** Goldens compare sorted key lists; contract exemplars are written and compared with `canonical_json` (sorted keys at every depth) or as `Value`s.
* New crates (`nyx-physics`, the three physics, `nyx-analysis`, `nyx-engine`) are formatted with `rustfmt` (the `crates/geom/rustfmt.toml` settings) and clippy-clean with `-D warnings`; the older crates are not yet (R23, decided in phase 9).

## Consequences

* The MCP build is part of `cargo build --workspace`; `ai/target` and `ai/Cargo.lock` are gone.
* The layering table is the single place that shows what the structure is allowed to be; a phase that removes an edge deletes a row.
* A parallel working session that adds a crate adds a row to the table (a one-line conflict at worst).

## Code

`Cargo.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `crates/nyx-engine/tests/layering.rs`, `crates/nyx-session`, `crates/nyx-mcp`, `crates/nyx-connect`, `crates/femcore/tests/golden_frames.rs` (sorted keys), `crates/nyx-mcp/tests/contracts.rs` (values).

## Contract

None of its own; the layering test is the guard.
decisions.title: One Cargo workspace for everything, and a test that holds the crate layering

# 28. `nyx-connect` is the only copy of the Connect logic, and its outputs are versioned contracts

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted by this change (phase 7a of the restructure plan: "merge `app/connect.rs` and `nyx-connect` into one"). Resolves ROUGH_SPOTS R07. Supersedes ADR 15 in part (the Connect menu keeping its own `.nyx-backup` logic in `app`).

## Context

`crates/app/src/connect.rs` (two clients, one `.nyx-backup` kept for good) and `crates/nyx-connect` (five hosts, a handshake test, a command line, a time-stamped backup per change) did the same job in two ways. They disagreed on the backup rule, the entry written (the app added `env: {}`), how a moved server is found, and the statuses. The `ai/` split that kept the app from calling the crate ended with ADR 26.

## Decision

* One crate, `nyx-connect`, library and binary. `app` depends on it and has no Connect code of its own; `nyx-mcp` may use it too. It stays a leaf of the layering table (`serde_json` only).
* Modules: `env` (where the machine keeps things; tests build an `Env` by hand), `hosts` (the table of five hosts and the entry each wants), `config` (status, connect, disconnect), `server` (finding `nyx-mcp`, the handshake probe), `report` (the JSON reports and their schema).
* **Rules for a host's config file** (tested in `tests/behaviour.rs`): only the `nyx` entry is touched; other keys and servers keep their order (`serde_json/preserve_order` is therefore a requirement of this crate, set in its own manifest); a file that is not plain JSON is never written; keys the user added to the `nyx` entry (an `env`) survive a reconnect; the file is replaced through a temporary file and a rename.
* **Backup**: the first time nyx changes a file the original is copied to `<name>.nyx-backup`; that copy is never overwritten, so it is the file as it was before nyx. (The crate's earlier `<name>.nyx-backup-<unix seconds>` could be overwritten by a second change in the same second and piled up; the app's rule won.)
* **Entry**: Claude Code gets `{type: stdio, command, args: [], env: {}}` (what `claude mcp add` writes and what the app wrote), VS Code `{type, command, args}` under `servers`, the others `{command, args}` under `mcpServers`.
* **Finding the server**: `NYX_MCP` (if set and wrong, nothing is found), then the folder of the running program; the menu then offers "Locate nyx-mcp...". That is the whole lookup of a shipped program. Only when the program sits in a cargo build tree (`is_cargo_build_tree`: its folder holds cargo's `deps` and `.fingerprint`, so `--release` developer builds count and an install never does) is the search widened to five folders in total, the program's own folder and its four parents, and for each of them its `target/release`. This was decided with paul on 2026-11-04 because a packaged install should not go looking in unrelated parent folders. The old compile-time guess from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` is dropped (it pointed at a target folder that the shared target directory of ADR 26 no longer is).
* **Report**: `nyx-connect list|connect|disconnect|test --json` prints `{"schema": "nyx-connect.<list|change|test>", "version": 1, ...}`. The JSON Schema is generated by `report::schema()` and checked in.

## Contracts

* `connect_hosts` v1 (`contracts/connect_hosts.v1.json`): per operating system, each host's config file relative to the home folder, servers key, hint and the entry written. AI hosts that registered nyx earlier read these entries; changing one is a version bump (ADR 19).
* `connect_report` v1 (`connect_report.v1.json` examples, `connect_report.v1.schema.json`). The test validates the examples and the live output of the built program against the schema with a small validator that refuses keywords it does not know. A new optional key keeps v1; a renamed, removed or re-typed key is v2.

## Consequences

* The Connect menu now lists every installed host (not only Claude Code and Desktop) and shows "no supported AI app found" when there is none.
* Tests that look at key order of a config file are on purpose here: the order is the behaviour, and the crate enables `preserve_order` itself, so ADR 26's rule (no key order in data-format tests) does not apply to them.
* A later engine command can call `nyx_connect::list` and return the `list` report as is.

## Code

`crates/nyx-connect/src/*`, `crates/nyx-connect/tests/{behaviour,contracts}.rs`, `crates/nyx-connect/examples/fake_mcp.rs`, `crates/app/src/app.rs` (Connect menu).

## Contract

`connect_hosts` v1, `connect_report` v1 (`docs/architecture/contracts/`).

# 29. Materials are TOML files with explicit units and a checked stiffness

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (gate G4 answered by paul on 2026-11-03: TOML). Supersedes the in-code material data of ADR 1 (`sapphire()`, `silicon()`) once the engine loads the library (phase 7).

## Context

`material.rs` described four crystal classes by named constants and carried two materials written in code. The plan asks for materials that are easy to write by hand and complete when needed: the full elastic matrix in the reduced Voigt form, the other tensor properties checked, units always written.

## Decision

* One material is one TOML file (`materials/*.toml` is the shipped library, loaded at run time by `Library::load_dir`; the code holds no copy). `format = 1` is required. Unknown keys are errors with a "did you mean" suggestion. Errors name the material, the table and the key, in plain words.
* **Units are never assumed.** A quantity is `"496.8 GPa"`, `{ value = .., unit = ".." }`, or a bare number next to a declared unit (`unit` in `[elastic]`, `<key>_unit` elsewhere). Dimensionless entries (Poisson's ratio, relative permittivity) are bare. A unit of the wrong kind is refused with what was expected. Everything inside the library is SI.
* **Stiffness** (`[elastic]`) in exactly one of five ways, all giving the same 6x6 matrix `c` (Pa, textbook Voigt order 1=xx 2=yy 3=zz 4=yz 5=xz 6=xy, engineering shear, crystal frame): class and independent constants (isotropic, cubic, hexagonal, trigonal, tetragonal, orthotropic, monoclinic with unique axis y or z, triclinic); the matrix (full 6x6 or the upper triangle as rows of 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1); the compliance as constants or matrix (the matrix inverse of the stiffness in Voigt form, so the shear entries carry the usual factors, which the loader derives); isotropic pairs (E and nu, lambda and mu, K and G).
* **Checks**: symmetry of a full matrix, entry by entry; positive definiteness through the eigenvalues of the Mandel-normalised matrix, with the Born criteria in the message for a cubic crystal; consistency with a declared class (the first offending entry and the relation it breaks); derived entries written anyway (`c66` of a hexagonal crystal) must agree; Poisson's ratio range. Permittivity and thermal conductivity must be positive in every direction, electrical conductivity not negative, expansion only symmetric.
* **Other tensors** (permittivity, thermal and electrical conductivity, expansion): one value, three (x y z), six (xx yy zz yz xz xy), a 3x3 array, or `{ perp, par }` for a uniaxial crystal about crystal z.
* Orientation is not a property of the material: the project places the crystal with Bunge angles (`Elastic::global`, `MaterialSpec::anisotropy`), as before.
* `MaterialSpec::to_toml` writes a file back (class and constants if the file gave them, the matrix otherwise; comments are not kept; numbers round-trip to 1e-12). `.nyx` archives embed the TOML text of the materials they use (engine, phase 7).
* The legacy `Stiffness` enum gains `General(M6)` so that a general matrix reaches the existing kernels through `Anisotropy`; `sapphire()` and `silicon()` stay until the engine loads the library, and a test pins them to the library files.

## Consequences

* A schema (`material_schema.v1.json`, generated by `material::schema`) documents the format; the loader is the authority. The contract test checks that the schema lists exactly the keys the loader accepts.
* Importing the refractiveindex.info format is not implemented (default of this phase); `source` records where numbers come from.
* Piezoelectric tensors, temperature-dependent stiffness and viscosity are not in format 1.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/material/{mod,units,reader,elastic,tensor,spec,schema}.rs`, `materials/*.toml`, `crates/femcore/tests/{materials,material_contract}.rs`, `docs/MATERIALS.md`.

## Contract

`material_schema.v1.json`, `material_kitchen_sink.v1.toml` and `.json` (see `contracts/README.md`).
decisions.title: Materials are TOML files with explicit units and a checked stiffness

# 3. geom is a lean, separate, analytic kernel that depends on nothing of nyx

Date: 2026-10-31

## Status

Accepted. Paul's decisions 1, 2, 3 and 6 in `docs/GEOM_HANDOFF.md` section 0; the STEP/Phase 5 plan in `GEOMETRY_ARCHITECTURE.md` was dropped on 2026-10-31.

## Context

A full CAD kernel was out of scope. The geometries nyx needs (strips, ribs, sloped walls, discs, rings, holes, photonic-crystal slabs, spheres) are analytic, and almost every photonic structure is a stack of prisms over 2D partitions.

## Decision

* `geom` is a separate crate, roughly 6k lines in the plan, with `serde` as the only required dependency (`rayon` optional, dev-dependencies `serde_json`, `proptest`). **No dependency on `femcore`, `faer`, the GUI or physics, ever.** The dependency direction is `app -> femcore -> geom`.
* Analytic geometry only: planes, cylinders, cones, spheres, tori; lines, circles, ellipses and procedural surface-surface curves. No NURBS, fillets, shells, sketch solver or assemblies.
* **Import is by mesh only.** No STEP, IGES or `Import` leaf.
* A 2.5D **layer-stack fast path** handles prismatic 3D models (mesh the 2D overlay of all layers, then extrude), which is also the periodic-friendly route.
* geom resolves *which* entities a rule picks; femcore decides what a condition means. Meshing is not in geom (display tessellation only).
* The curved-element refactor of the solvers is not geom's job. geom only makes it possible (exact queries, closest-point oracle).

## Consequences

* geom duplicates the small expression grammar of `femcore::expr` on purpose (rough spot R06).
* There is no 3D geom meshing pipeline: 3D adaptation starts from a tet mesh (extrusion or import) (`MISSING_FEATURES.md` section 3).
* The meshers use geom through `femcore::geomdrive` and `meshing::GeomOracle2`, never the reverse.
* The source is about 10.4k lines (`crates/geom/src`), well above the 6k of the plan; in practice the leanness that held is the dependency list, not the line count.

## Code

`crates/geom` (all of it), `crates/femcore/src/geomdrive.rs`, `meshing.rs`. History: `08dd007`.

## Contract

`contracts/geom_model` (see ADR 2). The dependency rule is checked by `crates/geom/tests/contracts.rs`, test `geom_depends_on_serde_only`.

# 30. Optical properties are dispersion models evaluated at the study wavelength

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (plan section 2, "Materials"; design in `DECISIONS_ROUND_3.md` section 4). Defaults used while paul has not answered the open questions: models constant, Sellmeier, Cauchy and tabulated first; no refractiveindex.info importer.

## Context

Optical materials were one number per domain. Photonic work needs `n(lambda)`, group index, loss and, for heated devices, `dn/dT`, per crystal axis, and must never produce a number outside the range where the data hold.

## Decision

* `[optical]` of a material holds models, not numbers: `constant` (n or eps, optional k), `sellmeier` (`n^2 = A + sum B x^2/(x^2 - C)`, `C` as squared resonance wavelengths or `lambda0` as wavelengths), `cauchy` (`n = sum c_i x^(-2 i)`), `tabulated` (`[wavelength, n]` or `[wavelength, n, k]` rows; monotone cubic (PCHIP) or linear interpolation of n and k against wavelength). A uniaxial crystal has `[optical.ordinary]` and `[optical.extraordinary]` (unique axis along crystal z), a biaxial one `[optical.x]`, `.y`, `.z`.
* **The wavelength unit is declared** (`wavelength_unit = "um"`) and is required whenever a coefficient, a table or a range uses it, so that published coefficients are pasted without conversion.
* **No silent extrapolation.** Formula models need a validity `range`; a table's range is its extent. A wavelength outside the range is an `OpticsError::OutOfRange` whose message names the range. A table may extend beyond its data only if the file says `extrapolate = "linear"`. At load, a Sellmeier resonance inside the range, a non-positive n over the range, an unsorted table, a negative k are refused.
* **Convention**: time dependence `e^{j omega t}`, complex index `n - j k`, relative permittivity `(n - j k)^2`. `Optical::index`, `d_index_d_lambda` (analytic for formulas, spline derivative for tables), `group_index`, `permittivity_diag` and `permittivity_global` (rotated into the wafer frame with the Bunge angles) take the wavelength in metres and an optional temperature.
* **Thermo-optic**: `dn_dT` (1/K) per axis shifts n by `dn_dT (T - T_ref)`, `reference_temperature` default 293.15 K; without a temperature argument nothing shifts.
* The study does not see a formula: the engine evaluates the material at the wavelength (a sweep loops in the engine) and hands the tensor to the physics, which declares the property it needs in its descriptors. Dispersive cavities (a nonlinear eigenproblem) are later work.

## Consequences

* Lorentz, Drude, Schott and Herzberger models are not implemented; `Dispersion` is an enum, so they are additions.
* Closed-form tests: fused silica (Malitson 1965: n(587.56 nm) = 1.458464, n(1.55 um) = 1.4440), sapphire (ordinary 1.7682 and extraordinary 1.7600 at 589.3 nm; 1.7462 and 1.7383 at 1.55 um), silicon (Li, 3.4757 at 1.55 um).

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/material/optics.rs`, `materials/{silicon,silica,sapphire,air}.toml`, `crates/femcore/tests/materials.rs`.

## Contract

As ADR 29 (the schema covers `[optical]`).
decisions.title: Optical properties are dispersion models evaluated at the study wavelength

# 31. femcore holds meshes, meshing and adaptation in three module trees

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (phase 2 of the restructure, step 1). Supersedes ADR 7 in part (where the ported mesher lives); the one-native-mesh decision (ADR 5) is carried out in later steps of phase 2.

## Context

Mesh code was spread over fifteen top-level modules of `femcore` (`mesh`, `view`, `cellmesh`, `geomdrive`, `mesher`, `mesher3d`, `refine3d`, `meshing`, `meshing_pml`, `pml3`, `physics_size`, `estimate`, `estimate3`) and a ported `meshers/` tree with its own mesh types, quality, fixtures, I/O, adaptation, validation and PML generator. Two feature streams (the mesher features and phase 2 itself) were going to edit the same files, and jj does not follow renames, so a move made later would turn every concurrent edit into a modify/delete conflict.

## Decision

* The files move, without any logic change, into three module trees (the first commit of the phase, `restructure-2-mesh` a4f8aa69):
  * `femcore::mesh`: `mod.rs` (`SimplexMesh`, was `mesh.rs`), `view`, `cellmesh` (the nyx `CellMesh`, legacy), `native` (the dimension-generic mesh, was `meshers/mesh.rs`), `cells` (was `meshers/cellmesh.rs`), `interop` (legacy), `io` (`.fmsh`), `quality`, `fixtures`.
  * `femcore::meshing`: `mod.rs` (`MeshPlan`, `mesh_model`, was `meshing.rs`), `geomdrive`, `mesher`, `mesher3d`, `refine3d`, `pml` (was `meshing_pml.rs`), `pml3`, `pml_box` (the structured PML generator, was `meshers/adapt/pml.rs`), `physics_size`, `validate` (the independent Helmholtz checker).
  * `femcore::adapt`: the metric adaptation (`metric`, `field`, `topo`, `ops`, `drive`, 2D and 3D), `estimate`, `estimate3`, `par`, `timer`.
* The old module paths do not survive: callers were rewritten in the same phase (second commit) and no re-export remains.
* `mesh::native` and `mesh::cells` stay beside the legacy types until the later steps of the phase delete `mesh::cellmesh` and `mesh::interop` and make the native mesh the only one (ADR 5). The move changes no behaviour; the tests, goldens and contract exemplars are unchanged.

## Consequences

* A mesher feature stream (the `FEATURE_DEPENDENCIES.md` items) can start from the move commit; its files have their final paths.
* `docs/ports/meshers/*` still describe the old `meshers::` paths; the provenance and licence notes remain valid.
* `meshers::par` is still its own module (`adapt::par`) until it is replaced by `femcore::par` (ADR 11).

`crates/femcore/src/{mesh,meshing,adapt}/`, `crates/femcore/src/lib.rs`.

# 32. One native mesh; `SimplexMesh` becomes the solver view of it

Date: 2026-11-04

## Status

Accepted (phase 2). Steps 1 and 2 are done (bookmark `restructure-2-mesh`); steps 3 to 5 are in progress; the removal of `SimplexMesh` is a phase 4 deliverable (below). Carries out ADR 5; resolves R01, R09 and R04 when done. Answers from paul (2026-11-04): 1-based labels everywhere, `interop` and the nyx `CellMesh`/`ElementType` deleted, one PML generator.

## Context

Four mesh types exist today: `mesh::SimplexMesh` (the solver contract: P1/P2 numbering, edges, 1-based labels), `mesh::cellmesh::CellMesh` (nyx's list-of-element-types form, boundary numbers 0-based), and the ported `mesh::native::SimplexMesh<D>` and `mesh::cells::CellMesh<D>` (dimension-generic, used by adaptation and the structured PML generator). `mesh::interop` converts between them and shifts boundary numbers. Callers of the bridge today: `adapt::{estimate, estimate3}`, `meshing::{mod, physics_size, pml, pml3}`, tests `adapt3d`, `contracts`, `meshing`, `split`. 0-based boundary numbers survive in `cellmesh`, in the `.fmsh`/view reader and in `meshing::pml`.

## Decision (target)

* `mesh::cells::CellMesh<D>` is the one mesh: points, per-cell-type connectivity with a domain number per cell, boundary elements with a boundary number, **both numbered from 1**; nodes per cell are defined by `(cell type, order)` (curved-node storage stays out, ADR 18).
* `mesh::native::SimplexMesh<D>` disappears: the adaptation works on a `CellMesh` whose cell types are all simplices.
* `mesh::SimplexMesh` stays as the solver's view (`SolverMesh` view): `SimplexMesh::from_cells(&CellMesh<3|2>, SplitMode)` splits non-simplex cells, builds edges and the unknown numbering. Kernels keep using it unchanged until they take cells directly.
* `mesh::cellmesh` (nyx), `ElementType` and `mesh::interop` are deleted.
* `meshing::pml` (2D structured PML for the nyx mesh) is rebuilt on `meshing::pml_box` (one generator); the PML output is a `CellMesh`.
* `Sizing` (wavelength per region, order, headroom) is defined in `femcore::meshing`; `physics_size` takes it instead of `ProblemSpec`; `nyx_physics::Sizing` re-exports it.

## Steps (each its own commit, suite at baseline after each)

1. Labels: 1-based boundary numbers in `pml_geom.rs`, the view reader and `from_cells` (delete the shift in `interop`); rewrite the `mesh_*` contract on purpose (ADR 19, `VERSIONS.md`).
2. `pml.rs`/`pml3.rs` return `cells::CellMesh`; `SimplexMesh::from_cells_split*` takes it; rebuild the hex/prism/quad cases of `tests/split.rs` on it.
3. **Amended (paul and the coordinator, 2026-11-04):** the adaptation keeps a private working mesh. `mesh::native` moves to `adapt::work` and `mesh::interop` is dissolved (the two conversion functions live in `adapt::work`, `pml_domains` in `meshing::pml_box`), so the public mesh vocabulary is `mesh::cells::CellMesh` plus the `SimplexMesh` solver view; adaptation is not ported onto `CellMesh` (cost below).
4. `mesh::cellmesh` and `mesh::interop` are gone (step 2 and 3); `adapt::work::SimplexMesh<D>` stays internal to `adapt`.
5. One PML generator; then `Sizing`; then rewrite the remaining `mesh_*` contracts and schemas and re-measure the benchmarks (best of three, idle machine).

## Consequences

Risk is in step 3 (adaptation speed and determinism; ADR 11) and in the numbering change of step 1 (anything that selects boundaries by number: `geomdrive` label maps, the app's selectors). Both are covered by the existing goldens and `tests/{meshers,adapt3d,meshing,physics_meshing,split}.rs`.

## Code

`crates/femcore/src/{mesh,meshing,adapt}/`.

## Contract

`mesh_*` in `crates/femcore/tests/contracts.rs` (rewritten at step 1 and 5).

## Amendment 2026-11-04: what stays simplex, and why (audit for paul's question "is the simplex still useful?")

* **Solver kernels need simplices today.** `dfs` (P1/P2 on triangles and tetrahedra), `sms` (P1/P2 triangles and tets), `ems` (Nedelec order 1 and 2 on triangles with P1/P2 phi), `ems3d` (Nedelec order 1 and 2 on tetrahedra, 6 and 20 dofs), `ems_pml`, `sms_pml`, periodic pairs, fields, analysis and `h5io` all read `mesh::SimplexMesh`, with its edge list and unknown numbering (28 files of `femcore/src` outside the mesh trees, plus `app/src/{state,worker}.rs`, `nyx-session/src/tools.rs`, `nyx-physics/src/lib.rs`). The kernels are being upgraded and extended by other threads; none reads quads, prisms or hexes, so structured PML layers are cut into simplices (`SimplexMesh::from_cells_split`).
* **Adaptation is intrinsically simplex.** Edge split, collapse, flip, smoothing, 3D edge removal and face flips, Rivara bisection and the Hessian recovery (`adapt/ops.rs` 421 lines, `ops3.rs` 863, `topo.rs` 434, `topo3.rs` 467, `estimate*.rs` 631) only exist for triangles and tetrahedra and run on their own topology structures (`Work2`, `Work3`). `metric.rs` (1009 lines) is dimension-generic algebra and does not touch a mesh. The mesh type appears only at entry and exit of those structures (about 21 `SimplexMesh` references and 35 field accesses in `topo*.rs`, `work.rs`, `field*.rs`, `estimate*.rs`, `drive*.rs`).
* **Mixed cells never enter adaptation.** The pipeline is: adapt the physical simplex mesh, then build the structured layers (`meshing::pml_box::build_pml`, which keeps the physical vertex ids), then split for the solvers. Porting the entry and exit of adaptation onto `CellMesh<D>` restricted to simplices would be a day of mechanical work (about 60 lines of conversion code) with no gain, so the private working type stays; a later `Work2::from_cells(&CellMesh<2>)` is possible without touching the algorithms.

## Phase 4 deliverable: remove `SimplexMesh`

When the physics crates exist (phase 4), each physics reads the native `CellMesh` and numbers its own unknowns (edges, faces, nodes for its element family). Then `mesh::SimplexMesh`, `from_cells_split` and the split report go away; quadrilaterals, prisms and hexahedra are solved natively, which also removes the unknowns that the cut adds in PML layers. Until then `SimplexMesh` is the solver view of the one mesh.

## Step 5 (done): one PML generator

`meshing::pml_box::build_pml` (2D quadrilateral layers, 3D prisms and hexahedra) is the only generator of structured layers. `meshing::pml_geom` (`structured_pml`, `structured_pml_native`) and `meshing::pml3` (`add_pml_3d`) are adapters: they turn a geom model's `Pml` feature, or a box-shaped tetrahedral mesh, into a `PmlSpec`, call `build_pml`, and cut the result for the simplex solvers. The inline mode (geom's `Pml` pieces meshed as ordinary regions, `PmlMode::Inline`) is a property of the geom model, not a second generator. Guarantee, now a contract test (`mesh_pml_generator_keeps_the_physical_vertex_and_cell_numbers`): the output mesh starts with the physical vertices and cells unchanged in id, order, connectivity and label, and the layers are appended; this is what the mesher feature chart item P3 (adapt the physical mesh, regenerate the layers, map fields back by id) needs, and it holds in 2D and 3D.

## Step 6 (done): the neutral `Sizing`

`femcore::meshing::Sizing { order, headroom, wavelengths: region name -> shortest wavelength }` is defined by the mesher (`meshing/sizing.rs`) and re-exported as `nyx_physics::Sizing`; the serde shape is unchanged, so the `physics_descriptors` contract did not move. `physics_size` computes element sizes from a `Sizing` (`cell_sizes_for`, `vertex_sizes_for`, `metrics_for`, `adapt_tets_for`); a size is `wavelength / headroom / points-per-wavelength`, relaxed in PML domains. Names are resolved to domain labels by the caller (`Sizing::resolve`; `sizing::label_names` for a mesh with numbers only). The functions that take a `ProblemSpec` (`cell_sizes`, `vertex_sizes`, `metrics`, `metrics_d`, `adapt_tets`, `mesh_for_problem`) remain as the adapter for the old kernels through `spec_sizing`; they are deleted in phase 4 when each physics crate answers `Physics::sizing`. One float detail: the headroom of an eigenfrequency study used to multiply the frequency before the wavelength was formed; it now divides the wavelength, which can differ in the last bit.
decisions.title: One native mesh; `SimplexMesh` becomes the solver view of it
